_comment: Defects in the training corpus itself, and which models carry their
consequences. Read by src/atr_training/corpus_defects.py; stamped onto the
model card by publish.py; checked by tests/test_corpus_defects.py.
A defect belongs here when the fix cannot end it: the code is corrected and
the weights trained before it are still on a share, still in an overlay,
still being cited. Until #35 that state lived in an issue table and in
hand-written `notes` on four HuggingFace cards, which is why a model could
be marked in one place and quoted in another.
retrain_pending - affected, no replacement exists yet. The open work.
superseded      - a retrain on the corrected corpus exists; name it in
withdrawn       - the weights are gone or were never published; nothing
to replace and nothing to warn about downstream.

defects.title: Ground truth truncated to the first word of each line
what: `pagexml.line_texts()` searched a TextLine's *descendants* for the first
Unicode element. Transkribus writes word segmentation as <Word> children,
each with its own TextEquiv/Unicode, and those precede the line's own
TextEquiv in document order — so word 1 came back and the rest of the line
was dropped. The same loop stood a second time in `line_boxes()`, which
labels the line crops for kraken and TrOCR.
The fix reads the line's own TextEquiv as a *direct child*, so a <Word>
can never take its place; the word texts are joined only when a line has
evidence: Re-preparing the same five datasets across the fix: 12,227,788 characters
before, 16,318,787 after, +33.5% — with page and line counts unchanged.
Per source: Rats- und Richtebücher +170.8%, AAEB +48.5%, Bullinger +5.5%,
The 19th-century corpus was affected too: parlamentsdienste-protokolle
after the fix — those two carried 10 and 6 characters per line before it.
In the models the symptom is a transcription that stops: on the Federal
Council test set (doi:10.5281/zenodo.4746342) the three 19th-century v1
models write only the first word on 18.4% / 22.2% / 29.3% of lines, and
289 lines break in all three with the same first word.
Proven, not inferred: all four 19th-century arms were retrained on the
corrected corpus and scored on the same benchmark on 2026-09-19. The collapse
goes to exactly 0 in every one of them — two model families, a 5x spread in
parameters, nothing changed but the corpus. One model reaching 0 leaves room
for a lucky run; four do not. docs/UBELIX_PLAN.md §24.

qwen3vl-german-xix-v1.note: v2 is the retrain on the corrected corpus: CER 0.2551 -> 0.0765 on the 2,751 Federal Council lines, and 507 collapsed lines (18.4%) -> 0.

qwen3.5-2b-german-xix-v1.note: Same retrain and benchmark: CER 0.2937 -> 0.0895, and 611 collapsed lines (22.2%) -> 0. docs/UBELIX_PLAN.md §24.
